newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Independent group says Albanian local polls fair.
newsitem.headline: Independent group says Albanian local polls fair.

text.p: An independent group that monitored local elections in Albania said on Thursday that the vote was fair and marked an improvement on general elections earlier this year.
"Many technical elements in the October 20 elections were far more positive than those of May 26," said Miranda Grace, head of the U.S.-funded Society for Democratic Culture (SHKD).
"We conclude the October 20 elections were calm, just and honest," she told a news conference.
Preliminary results said the ruling Democratic Party won control of more than 61 percent of city halls, including Tirana, and 58 percent of commune seats.
The socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, emerged with six percent of city halls and commune seats, down from 50 percent in 1992 local elections.
About 1,500 monitors from the Albanian-based Society for Democratic Culture visited a third of the 4,665 polling stations on election day and watched the count at 772 stations.
"We found more votes in the ballot box than the number of registered voters in some polling stations but the number was not big enough to change the result," Gace said.

She described the pre-election campaign as calm and said voter registers were published on time in 60 percent of constituencies. She also praised the make-up of electoral commissions and the method of sealing and signing ballots.
But she regretted that her organisation was forced to cut the number of its monitors by a quarter because of government legislation ruling that observers must be aged at least 25.
Albanian general elections in May and June ended in disarray after most opposition parties withdrew alleging vote-rigging.
